mechanism: A VM with root sees the driver directly; containers do not.
summary: First lab GPU session, 2026-10-03, Verda 1H200.141S.44V in FIN-02 ($4.83/h), image ubuntu-24.04-cuda-12.8-open-docker, driver 580.126.09, torch 2.14.0+cu130, login as root. Facts about the venue: `nvidia-smi -lgc 1980,1980` succeeds (root on a VM), so measurement clock state is controllable, unlike the container venues; `nsys` 2024.6 ships in the image; `apt-get install nsight-compute` works and `ncu` 2025.1.1 reads SM throughput counters (73.8% on a 4096x4096 matmul) with no permission error; the per-100ms nvidia-smi sampler (gpu.csv) works. `scripts/gpu_tests/checks.py`: 4/4 paged-attention parity checks pass on H200. Setup from a fresh VM takes about a minute with uv. Known problem (PR #83): Verda hibernate removes the instance from GET /instances, so `lab.vm stop` never sees `stopped`; end a session by deleting the instance and its OS volume. The passphrase-protected default ssh key fails under BatchMode; use a passphrase-free key (`LAB_VM_KEYFILE=~/.ssh/lab_ed25519.pub`).
title: Verda 1x H200 VM: clocks lock, Nsight Compute counters read, nsys present; hibernate hides the instance
triggers: choosing a GPU venue for measurement
